articles.title: Building Fair Rhythm-Game Judgement Windows in JavaScript
articles.excerpt: A rhythm game can feel unfair even when its note chart is correct. The usual cause is timing logic that mixes wall-clock time, animation frames, and audio playback position. A fair judgement system ne…
articles.body: A rhythm game can feel unfair even when its note chart is correct. The usual cause is timing logic that mixes wall-clock time, animation frames, and audio playback position. A fair judgement system needs one authoritative clock and explicit windows for each result. This walkthrough builds a compact JavaScript model suitable for a browser rhythm game or prototype. Use the audio clock Do not advance song time by adding the duration of each animation frame. Frames can be delayed by background tabs, garbage collection, or a busy device. Instead, sample the playback clock on every frame. function songTime ( audioContext , startedAt , offset = 0 ) { return audioContext . currentTime - startedAt + offset ; } The same clock should drive note positions and input judgement.
articles.author: SkyWalker

articles.title: Implementing FreeCell SuperMoves: Capacity Rules and Edge Cases
articles.excerpt: FreeCell looks simple until a player tries to move a long descending run and the interface refuses. The useful programming lesson is that a legal “supermove” is not a special card rule. It is a compac…
articles.body: FreeCell looks simple until a player tries to move a long descending run and the interface refuses. The useful programming lesson is that a legal “supermove” is not a special card rule. It is a compact way of representing a sequence of ordinary single-card moves through temporary storage. This article derives a small capacity calculator that can be used in a browser-based FreeCell implementation, a rules explainer, or automated tests. The basic capacity rule Let: F be the number of empty free cells. C be the number of empty tableau columns that may be used as temporary storage. The destination column is not counted as empty storage.

articles.title: Who sells the book when the customer asks an AI? Romania's book market across 5 AI engines
articles.excerpt: When someone asks ChatGPT "which online bookstore should I use for children's books?", they get one answer, not ten blue links. So we measured who is inside that answer. We put 18 real purchase questi…
articles.body: When someone asks ChatGPT "which online bookstore should I use for children's books?" , they get one answer , not ten blue links. So we measured who is inside that answer. We put 18 real purchase questions to five AI engines — ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and Google AI Overviews — in Romanian, from Romania, across two complete weekly runs. No question contained a brand name. Every brand that appears was named by the engine on its own. The result: 180 analysed answers, 247 brand mentions, 21 tracked brands, 422 distinct cited domains. The headline finding is the one we did not expect. 58% of answers name nobody Out of 180 answers, only 75 (42%) mention any of the 21 major brands in the market.
articles.author: Dan Cristian

articles.title: Spec-driven development with AI agents: constitutions, checkpoints, and handoffs
articles.excerpt: AI coding agents are strangely lopsided. Hand one a well-scoped task and it writes better code, faster, than I do. Hand it a large feature, the kind that takes days and touches a dozen files across se…
articles.body: AI coding agents are strangely lopsided. Hand one a well-scoped task and it writes better code, faster, than I do. Hand it a large feature, the kind that takes days and touches a dozen files across several layers, and the failure mode changes. The context window fills up and quality quietly degrades (AKA context rot ). A fresh session, missing the history, confidently invents an API that never existed. And even when the code is good, you're left staring at a 3,000-line diff you can't meaningfully review. Those failures are not solved by the model alone. They are largely a process problem. The backbone I work inside isn't mine and isn't novel: a constitution, specs, and deliberately stabilized plans. It's spec-driven development, which has been around in various shapes for years.

But the idea of a kid-focused daily podcast built from family calendars remains a plausible application of existing capabilities , not an announced OpenAI feature. The concept is straightforward: an AI assistant receives permitted calendar context, identifies relevant events such as a soccer game or birthday, and generates a concise script for a school-run briefing. Calendar access is the important enabling layer. OpenAI has documented ways for ChatGPT to work with calendar information, although its published materials do not describe a packaged family-oriented briefing or podcast product.

articles.title: XCOM and Gloomhaven's creators say video game and tabletop collabs can save the industry
articles.excerpt: An easier development path, built-in audience, and licensing fees can be a lifeline in a time of layoffs and high tariffs
articles.body: The gaming industry is in crisis. Layoffs at Xbox have led to still more layoffs from the studios Microsoft ditched. Bungie significantly reduced its staff right after releasing its final update for Destiny 2 and Epic Games cut 1,000 employees in March due to a downturn in Fortnite engagement. The tabletop industry has its own set of problems. Pathfinder publisher Paizo had to restructure after its book distributor Diamond Comics declared bankruptcy and CMON had layoffs , citing rising tariffs as it struggled to fulfill crowdfunding campaigns. The cancellation of projects like Plaid Hat’s The Monolith and the Altered expansion Roots of Corruption even after they achieved their crowdfunding goals further demonstrated the industry’s financing problems.

articles.title: 'Flight of the Navigator' at 40: the Disney space movie that messed with time dilation long before 'Interstellar'
articles.excerpt: 40 years later, 'Flight of the Navigator' remains an ambitious cult classic that refuses to speak down to its target audience.
articles.body: Despite Han Solo's protestations to the contrary, travelling faster than light on screen is usually just as straightforward as dusting crops. So whether you're in "Star Wars", "Star Trek" or "Battlestar Galactica", jumping to hyperspace, going to warp or spooling up the FTL really is as simple as popping out to the store. In fact, Albert Einstein's time-dilating general theory of relativity tends to be little more than an afterthought, with films highlighting the inconveniences of interstellar travel definitely in the minority. For this reason, the very existence of "Flight of the Navigator" is even more improbable than its premise.

articles.excerpt: We just got an amazing new view of SpaceX's Starship vehicle in space, thanks to one of the company's Starlink V3 broadband satellites.
articles.body: We just got an amazing new view of SpaceX's Starship vehicle, thanks to one of the company's next-gen Starlink satellites. Starship , the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, launched on its 13th test flight from South Texas last Friday (July 24). The suborbital jaunt was similar in many respects to past Starship test missions, with one big exception: This time, the vehicle deployed a batch of functional, next-gen Starlink internet satellites into space. Six of those "Starlink V3" spacecraft carried cameras, so that SpaceX could get good views of the heat shield on Starship's upper stage, which is known as Starship, or simply Ship. The satellites did that job and more, capturing amazing views of Ship as it cruised away from them high above Earth .

articles.title: How do supermassive black holes grow? AI finds 7 spacetime-warping 'quasars' that could help solve the mystery
articles.excerpt: Astronomers found seven rare quasar gravitational lens candidates using AI, providing a powerful new tool for studying black hole and galaxy evolution.
articles.body: Some of the brightest objects in the universe may also hold the key to understanding how galaxies evolve — especially when gravity transforms them into giant cosmic magnifying glasses. Using artificial intelligence to search through data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), astronomers have identified seven promising candidates for quasars acting as gravitational lenses — natural cosmic magnifying glasses created when a massive object's gravity bends and magnifies light from a more distant object. These unusual systems could help researchers better understand how actively growing supermassive black holes evolve, according to a statement from Ohio State University.

articles.title: Claude published malicious code to the Internet and attacked 3 real companies
articles.excerpt: Had the hacks used conventional methods, someone would likely go to prison.
articles.body: Anthropic said its Claude-based security models gained unauthorized access to the sensitive production environments of three outside organizations during internal testing designed to measure the models’ offensive cyber capabilities. The events, which Anthropic revealed Thursday , are the second revelation in 10 days that AI models from the world’s wealthiest providers have trespassed into protected networks, an offense that, in more traditional hacking scenarios, could land the human behind the keyboard in prison for years. Earlier this month, OpenAI said its security models exploited a zero-day vulnerability for use in breaking into the network of Hugging Face, a platform for open source machine-learning models and AI datasets.
